summary:
The store was a Vite + React SPA that rendered nothing without JavaScript, so AI agents saw a blank page. All fixes are generated at build time from the store's own catalogue (`public/api/products.json`) — no data was copied by hand and no dependencies were added.

- **Build script (`scripts/generate-static.mjs`)**: a Node script (no new dependencies) that runs after `vite build` (wired into the `build` npm script) and reads the catalogue JSON. It reuses the site's compiled stylesheet plus header/footer markup so generated pages match the store's design.
- **Plain-HTML product pages**: one page per product at `/products/<handle>/` with the name in an `<h1>`, price as text (₹), description, image, stock status and an "Add to cart" link.
- **Homepage and `/shop/` listing**: a plain HTML product list (name, price, link, stock) injected inside `<div id="root">` of the built SPA shell, so agents read it and the React app replaces it when it boots — humans see no change.
- **Machine-readable data**: Product JSON-LD (name, description, image, sku, url, offers with price/currency/availability, `<` escaped as `\u003c`) on every product page, plus `/sitemap.xml` (homepage, shop, all product URLs) and `/llms.txt` (store summary, product list with prices, and a "How to buy" section).
- **No-JS add to cart**: each product page links to `/buy/<handle>/`, a generated cart page ("Your cart", the item with quantity 1 and price) whose "Checkout" link goes to the shareable checkout page.
- **Shareable checkout link**: `/checkout/<handle>/` is generated with the order summary in plain HTML and as an SPA shell, so the existing React checkout form takes over in the browser. `Checkout.tsx` now also fills the cart from the URL — `/checkout/<handle>` or `/checkout?items=<slug>:<qty>,…` — so a link opens with the same items on any device, no cookies. A `/checkout/:handle` route was added; nothing else in the app's behaviour changed.

Result: the AI shopping Tester now passes 5/5 steps (previously 0/5). Note: `robots.txt` is still absent — the owner didn't select that fix, so it was left alone.
